topics.title: Travel in a variety of directions using basic locomotor skills and demonstrate understanding of personal and general space

subtopics.title: Travel in a variety of directions using basic locomotor skills and demonstrate understanding of personal and general space (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Move safely in a large group without bumping into others or falling while using locomotor skills.
Travel forward and sideways while changing directions quickly in response to a signal.
Perform movements to the rhythm of music.
Develop motor control and balance for a range of physical activities, such as walking, propelling a wheelchair or mobility device, skipping, running, climbing, and hopping.

subtopics.title: Travel in a variety of directions using basic locomotor skills and demonstrate understanding of personal and general space (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Develop motor coordination and skill in using objects for a range of physical activities, such as pulling, throwing, catching, kicking, bouncing or hitting balls, and riding a tricycle.
Demonstrate the relationship of under, over, behind, next to, through, right, left, up, down, forward, backward, and in front of by using the body and an object.

Understand movement concepts, such as control of the body, how the body moves (such as awareness of space and directionality), and that the body can move independently or in coordination with other objects.

topics.title: Recognize the positive feelings experienced during and after physical activity

subtopics.title: Recognize the positive feelings experienced during and after physical activity

outcomes.text: Participate in activities that increase the heart rate.
Participate in activities that require stretching the muscles.
Begin to understand how daily activity and healthy behavior promote overall personal health and safety.
Identify physical activity opportunities inside and outside of school.

topics.title: Demonstrate understanding of positive social interaction with teachers and peers

subtopics.title: Demonstrate understanding of positive social interaction with teachers and peers

outcomes.text: Demonstrate listening to the teacher during group activities.
Demonstrate sharing and taking turns when with participating with peers.
Follow directions to simple activities.
Recognize basic class rules and protocols.
Individuals recognize that rules make situations and activities safe and run more smoothly.

topics.title: Understand basic safety rules and principles

subtopics.title: Understand basic safety rules and principles

outcomes.text: Follow teacher directions for safe participation in physical activity.
Follow basic health and safety rules and respond appropriately to harmful or unsafe situations.
Communicate an understanding of the importance of health and safety routines and rules.

topics.title: Demonstrate body and spatial awareness through movement

subtopics.title: Demonstrate body and spatial awareness through movement (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Travel within a large group without bumping into others or falling while using a variety of locomotor skills.
Demonstrate contrasts between slow and fast speeds while using locomotor skills.
Travel in straight, curved, and zigzag pathways.
Move in opposition and alternately.

subtopics.title: Demonstrate body and spatial awareness through movement (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Move synchronously with others.
Participate in chase-and-flee activities that include various spatial relationships.
Jump over a stationary rope several times in succession using forward-andback and side-to-side movement patterns.

topics.title: Locate and move the major parts of the body

subtopics.title: Locate and move the major parts of the body

outcomes.text: Move specified body parts in response to a variety of sensory cues such as auditory or visual.
Identify body planes such as front, back, and side.
Create shapes at high, medium, and low levels by using hands, arms, torso, feet, and legs in a variety of combinations.

topics.title: Understand that physical activity increases the heart rate, making the heart stronger

subtopics.title: Understand that physical activity increases the heart rate, making the heart stronger

outcomes.text: Identify the heart rate as an indicator of physical activity.
Sustain physical activity for short periods of time.
Identify activities that will increase the heart rate.

topics.title: Demonstrate respect for self, others, and equipment

subtopics.title: Demonstrate respect for self, others, and equipment

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the characteristics of sharing.
Identify feelings that result from participation in physical activity.
Participate as a leader and follower.
Help to manage equipment.
Play without interfering with others.

topics.title: Demonstrate the ability to follow directions

subtopics.title: Demonstrate the ability to follow directions

outcomes.text: Start and stop on an auditory and visual signal.
Follow a simple series of instructions for an activity
Speak at appropriate times.
Follow established class protocols.

topics.title: Apply safe practices, rules, and procedures

subtopics.title: Apply safe practices, rules, and procedures

outcomes.text: Demonstrate safety awareness when using materials.
Participate in activity without colliding into other students, objects, and surroundings.
Identify proper footwear for physical education.

topics.title: Demonstrate basic locomotor and non-locomotor skills and rhythmic and cross-lateral movements

subtopics.title: Demonstrate basic locomotor and non-locomotor skills and rhythmic and cross-lateral movements (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Move in different directions and at high, medium, and low levels in space.
Demonstrate locomotor movements in a variety of pathways and levels.
Travel in forward and sideways directions using a variety of locomotor and non-locomotor patterns, and change direction quickly in response to a signal.
Perform a simple dance step in keeping with a specific tempo.
Travel to a variety of rhythms changing time, force, and flow.

subtopics.title: Demonstrate basic locomotor and non-locomotor skills and rhythmic and cross-lateral movements (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Manipulate objects such as jump ropes, scarves, hoops, and balls.
Balance at different levels on different body parts.
Demonstrate both static and dynamic balances.
Perform rhythmical movements using small musical aids.

topics.title: Demonstrate fundamental manipulative skills

subtopics.title: Demonstrate fundamental manipulative skills

outcomes.text: Standing in place, dribble a ball continuously with one’s dominant hand.
Throw an object with an overhand or underhand motion while stepping forward in opposition.
Toss a ball to oneself using the underhand throw pattern, and catch it before it bounces
Catch a thrown large object with both hands.
Kick a stationary object using a simple kicking pattern.
Use body parts and light implements to strike stationary and moving objects.

topics.title: Establish a beginning movement vocabulary

subtopics.title: Establish a beginning movement vocabulary

outcomes.text: Distinguish between a jog and a run, a hop and a jump, and a gallop and a slide.
Respond appropriately to a variety of cues.
Recognize personal space, high and low levels, fast and slow speeds, straight, curved, and zigzag pathways, balance, and twist.
Distinguish between personal space, general space, and boundaries.

topics.title: Identify the body’s normal reactions to moderate and vigorous physical activity

subtopics.title: Identify the body’s normal reactions to moderate and vigorous physical activity

outcomes.text: Identify basic exercises that help to strengthen various muscles of the body, such as push-ups, curl-ups, squats, planks, mountain climbers.
Identify physical activities that require strong muscles.
Identify heart beating faster, harder breathing, and sweating as reactions to exercise.

topics.title: Work independently and with others to complete work

subtopics.title: Work independently and with others to complete work

outcomes.text: Identify and demonstrate acceptable responses to challenges, successes, and failures.
Invite others to use equipment before repeating a turn.
Identify and demonstrate the attributes of being an effective partner or group member in physical activity.
Help another student share space effectively.

topics.title: Follow the rules of an activity

subtopics.title: Follow the rules of an activity

outcomes.text: Perform movements within given parameters and guidelines.
Develop rules for an activity with teacher assistance, and participate in the activity while following the rules.
Follow the rules for simple games and activities.
Accept responsibility for one’s behavior in a game situation.

topics.title: Develop movement control for safe participation in games and physical activities

subtopics.title: Develop movement control for safe participation in games and physical activities

outcomes.text: Recognize appropriate safety practices in general space (e.g., throwing objects when appropriate, only throwing objects when others are not in the direct line of the throw).
Demonstrate the ability to follow verbal and nonverbal instruction.

topics.title: Demonstrate the elements of movement in combination with a variety of locomotor skills

subtopics.title: Demonstrate the elements of movement in combination with a variety of locomotor skills

outcomes.text: Demonstrate skipping, hopping, galloping, and sliding while transitioning on command.
Demonstrate smooth transitions between sequential motor skills such as running into a jump.
Move using the concepts of space awareness and movement control to run, hop, and skip in different ways in a large group without bumping into others or falling.
Identify major characteristics of the skills of walking, running, jumping, hopping, and leaping.
Correctly identify the locomotor, non-locomotor, or manipulative skill in a variety of activities.

topics.title: Demonstrate control and balance in traveling and weight-bearing activities using a variety of body parts and implements

subtopics.title: Demonstrate control and balance in traveling and weight-bearing activities using a variety of body parts and implements

outcomes.text: Move to even and uneven beats using various locomotor movements.
Create a routine that includes two types of body rolls such as a log roll, egg roll, shoulder roll, or forward roll and a stationary balance position after each roll.
Jump rope repeatedly.
Throw, catch, strike, and trap objects while stationary or moving with a partner.
Balance objects on various body parts while in various positions.
Demonstrate static and dynamic balance on lines or low beams and benches.

topics.title: Use feedback to improve performance

subtopics.title: Use feedback to improve performance

outcomes.text: Use instructor feedback to identify strengths and weaknesses.
Identify modifications to improve performance of a skill or physical movement.

topics.title: Identify healthy habits for personal wellness

subtopics.title: Identify healthy habits for personal wellness

outcomes.text: Explain the fuel requirements of the body during physical activity and inactivity.
Identify healthy food choices to fuel the body.
Determine the proper amount of sleep to get every night.
Identify changes in the body during exercise and how that makes you feel.
Identify feelings resulting from challenges, successes, and failures in physical activity.
Describe the role of water as an essential nutrient for the brain and body.

topics.title: Demonstrate positive and helpful behavior and words toward other students

subtopics.title: Demonstrate positive and helpful behavior and words toward other students

outcomes.text: Describe how positive social interaction can make physical activity with others more fun.
Participate in a variety of group settings without distracting behavior.
Encourage others by using verbal and nonverbal communication.

topics.title: Apply rules, procedures, and safe practices in the classroom

subtopics.title: Apply rules, procedures, and safe practices in the classroom

outcomes.text: Maintain safety within personal space while using implements.
Follow safety rules in the gymnasium and on the playground.

topics.title: Demonstrate a variety of motor patterns in simple combinations while participating in activities, games, and sports

subtopics.title: Demonstrate a variety of motor patterns in simple combinations while participating in activities, games, and sports

outcomes.text: Demonstrate changes of pathways, levels, forces, and direction with manipulatives.
Dribble while changing speed and direction.
Demonstrate throwing, catching, striking or trapping in an activity.
Demonstrate skills of chasing, fleeing, and dodging to avoid others.

topics.title: Perform cross lateral and rhythmic exercises that make a brain-body connection

subtopics.title: Perform cross lateral and rhythmic exercises that make a brain-body connection (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Describe, create, and demonstrate movements that require crossing the midline.
Perform successfully a variety of jump-rope skills using both short and long ropes, and jump to various tempos.
Perform jumping, tossing, dribbling, or catching to music or rhythmic beat.
Perform a basic tinikling step to 3/4 time (close, tap, and tap).

subtopics.title: Perform cross lateral and rhythmic exercises that make a brain-body connection (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Balance demonstrating momentary stillness in symmetrical and nonsymmetrical shapes on a variety of body parts.
Perform forward and backward rolls with variation.
Combine two or more rotational skills.

topics.title: Demonstrate understanding of how the use of self-assessment aids in skill development

subtopics.title: Demonstrate understanding of how the use of self-assessment aids in skill development

outcomes.text: Use self-feedback to identify strengths and weaknesses.
Use instructor or self-feedback to make adjustments that will improve performance.

topics.title: Identify the benefits of sustained physical activity that causes increased heart rate and heavy breathing

subtopics.title: Identify the benefits of sustained physical activity that causes increased heart rate and heavy breathing (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Explain why the body perspires, the heart beats faster and breathing increases when participating in moderate to vigorous physical activity.
Describe the relationship among the heart, lungs, muscles, blood, and oxygen during physical activity.
Identify several moderate to vigorous physical activities (formal or informal) that provide personal pleasure.
Locate heart rate on at least two different pulse points on the body.

subtopics.title: Identify the benefits of sustained physical activity that causes increased heart rate and heavy breathing (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Discuss how drinking an adequate amount of water before, during, and after physical activity keeps the body hydrated.
Demonstrate the ability to understand the concept of pacing during cardiovascular endurance activity.
Explain how the intensity and duration of exercise affect fuel use during physical activity.

topics.title: Understand that the body is composed of water, muscle, bones, organs, fat, and other tissues

subtopics.title: Understand that the body is composed of water, muscle, bones, organs, fat, and other tissues

outcomes.text: Identify the location of the lungs and heart.
Identify muscles and fat.
Feel your heart beat after moderate to vigorous physical activity.
Compare heart rate before, during, and after exercise, and explain that increasing the heart rate during physical activity strengthens the heart muscles.
Identify physical activities that cause the heart to beat faster.

topics.title: Demonstrate positive social behaviors during physical activity

subtopics.title: Demonstrate positive social behaviors during physical activity

outcomes.text: Identify the positive behaviors of self and others.
Congratulate teammates and opponents upon conclusion of a game or activity.
Follow directions, activity-specific rules, procedures, and etiquette with few reminders
Encourage others regularly, and refrain from put-down statements.
Ask a partner to participate in a physical activity.
Congratulate friends for performing a skill correctly.

topics.title: Identify ways to prevent injuries during physical activity

subtopics.title: Identify ways to prevent injuries during physical activity

outcomes.text: Recognize how injuries can occur during physical activity.
Understand how activities can affect safety of self and others.

topics.title: Identify the major characteristics of mature locomotor, non-locomotor, manipulative, and rhythmic skills

subtopics.title: Identify the major characteristics of mature locomotor, non-locomotor, manipulative, and rhythmic skills (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Dribble and pass an object to a moving receiver.
Throw, catch, and kick to self or a partner.
Jump and land for height and distance using mature form.
Use a variety of manipulatives to throw to a moving target, making the needed adjustments for skill improvement.
Create a rhythmic routine, including gymnastics, creative dance, or jump rope.

subtopics.title: Identify the major characteristics of mature locomotor, non-locomotor, manipulative, and rhythmic skills (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Demonstrate balances with control on a variety of objects such as a balance board, balance beam, or skates (ice or in-line).
Transfer weight from feet to hands at fast and slow speeds using large extensions such as mule kicks, handstands, or cartwheels.
Distinguish and describe the similarities and differences of manipulative skills such as basketball and soccer dribbling or overhand and underhand.
Demonstrate efficient patterns of striking with and without an implement.

topics.title: Provide and receive feedback to and from peers using the major characteristics of mature locomotor and manipulative skills

subtopics.title: Provide and receive feedback to and from peers using the major characteristics of mature locomotor and manipulative skills

outcomes.text: Use peer assessment tools to recognize and evaluate the critical elements of movement in a variety of physical activities.
Identify critical elements of movement skills when watching a video for self or peer assessment.

topics.title: Explain how the health-related fitness components are used to improve physical fitness

subtopics.title: Explain how the health-related fitness components are used to improve physical fitness

outcomes.text: Identify and demonstrate flexibility exercises for major muscle groups.
Identify health-related components of fitness and demonstrate an exercise that positively impacts each component.
Measure and record personal heart rate before, during, and after moderate to vigorous exercise.
Identify and perform specific exercises that can be done to improve the muscular strength and endurance of various muscle groups.
Explain the benefits of having good cardiovascular endurance.
Recognize healthy and balanced meals and snacks designed to enhance the performance of physical activities.

topics.title: Analyze opportunities for participating in physical activity and actively engage in teacher-directed and independent activities

subtopics.title: Analyze opportunities for participating in physical activity and actively engage in teacher-directed and independent activities

outcomes.text: Understand the importance of participation in fitness-enhancing physical activities such as gymnastic clubs, community-sponsored youth sports, or activity clubs.
Demonstrate appropriate warm-up procedures before participation in vigorous physical activity.

topics.title: Assess and take responsibility for personal behavior and stress management

subtopics.title: Assess and take responsibility for personal behavior and stress management

outcomes.text: Act in a safe and healthy manner when confronted with negative peer pressure during physical activity.
Set a personal goal to improve a skill and work toward that goal.
Describe and demonstrate responsible behavior and decision-making while participating in physical activity.
Demonstrate respect for the person who is officiating.
Recognize that physical activity can be used as a stress management technique.

topics.title: Demonstrate knowledge of safe practices in a physical activity setting

subtopics.title: Demonstrate knowledge of safe practices in a physical activity setting

outcomes.text: Explain safety considerations prior to participation in lead-up games.
Demonstrate the safe use of implements.
Differentiate between safe and unsafe participation and environment
Display safe and responsible behavior while engaging in fitness activities.
Develop with an instructor’s help the safety rules for physical education.

topics.title: Demonstrate mature form for all basic locomotor, non-locomotor, manipulative, and rhythmic skills

subtopics.title: Demonstrate mature form for all basic locomotor, non-locomotor, manipulative, and rhythmic skills (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Throw and catch an object demonstrating both accuracy and force.
Punt a ball dropped from the hands at a target.
Dribble a ball (by hand or foot) while preventing another person from stealing the ball.
Volley an object continuously with a partner.

outcomes.text: Strike an object consecutively in a competitive or cooperative game.
Demonstrate correct steps and patterns for dance. (e.g., square, folk, modern, contemporary).
Perform a short or long rope jump routine with a partner or small group.
Develop and refine a gymnastics or creative dance sequence, and demonstrate smooth transitions.

topics.title: Demonstrate understanding of how to combine and apply movement concepts and principles to learn and develop motor skills

subtopics.title: Demonstrate understanding of how to combine and apply movement concepts and principles to learn and develop motor skills

outcomes.text: Use basic understanding of the knowledge of strategies in activity settings such as moving to open space to receive a pass or intercepting an object.
Analyze and correct errors in movement patterns, and provide and use feedback from a peer or instruction technology.
Develop a cooperative movement game that uses locomotor skills, object manipulation, and an offensive strategy, and teach the game to another person.

topics.title: Understand why feedback can improve performance

subtopics.title: Understand why feedback can improve performance

outcomes.text: Analyze and correct errors in throw, catch, hand dribble, foot dribble, striking a ball, and volley, and demonstrate control and accuracy.
Analyze and correct errors in non-locomotor and locomotor movements.
Analyze and use basic offensive and defensive strategies, and apply rules in modified games and activities.
Analyze and demonstrate a variety of social, folk, square, modern, jazz, or creative dance.

topics.title: Demonstrate understanding of skill-related components of fitness and how they affect physical performance

subtopics.title: Demonstrate understanding of skill-related components of fitness and how they affect physical performance

outcomes.text: Identify and demonstrate exercises that are used to develop agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time, or speed.
Create a plan using the six skill-related components to improve performance in a chosen activity.

topics.title: Set personal goals for improving health-related fitness

outcomes.text: Explain how the five health-related fitness components (body composition, cardiovascular endurance, flexibility, muscular endurance, and muscular strength) affect ability to participate normally in everyday activities.
Compare results of fitness testing to personal health status and ability to perform various activities.
Develop short term and long-term fitness goals.

subtopics.title: Set personal goals for improving health-related fitness (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Identify activities that will help to improve cardio-respiratory, muscular endurance, muscular strength, flexibility, and body composition.
Accurately take a pulse at rest and during exercise.
Identify the components of the FITT principle (frequency, intensity, time, type).

topics.title: Identify personal activity interests and abilities and take responsibility for individual and team performance

outcomes.text: Accept responsibility for one’s own performance without blaming others.
Respond to winning and losing in socially appropriate ways.
Develop confidence in self and others in a physical activity setting.
Try new activities and connect hard work and practice to success.

topics.title: Work cooperatively and productively in a group

outcomes.text: Establish and accomplish goals in both cooperative and competitive activities.
Identify and define the role of each participant in a group physical activity.
Analyze possible solutions to a problem in a group physical activity, and come to a consensus on the best solution.
Demonstrate the ability to resolve conflicts with peers.

topics.title: Implement safety procedures in the utilization of space and equipment

subtopics.title: Implement safety procedures in the utilization of space and equipment

outcomes.text: Identify and participate in safe warm-up and cool-down activities.
Review components of safe participation and what constitutes a safe environment.
Follow the rules of activities to maintain safe playing conditions.
Describe safe and unsafe practices for a variety of physical activities.

topics.title: Demonstrate beginning skills for a variety of activities, games, and sports

outcomes.text: Volley an object repeatedly with a partner.
Strike a ball continually against a wall and with a partner, using a paddle for the forehand stroke and backhand stroke.
Strike an object consistently, using a body part and an implement so that the object travels in the intended direction at the desired height.

subtopics.title: Demonstrate beginning skills for a variety of activities, games, and sports (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Throw an object accurately and with applied force, using the underhand, overhand, and sidearm movement (throw) patterns.
Combine relationships, levels, speed, direction, and pathways in complex individual and group physical activities.

topics.title: Participate in activities that require problem-solving, cooperation, and team-building

subtopics.title: Participate in activities that require problem-solving, cooperation, and team-building

outcomes.text: Participate in initiative and cooperative activities.

subtopics.title: Demonstrate beginning strategies for a variety of activities, games, or sports

outcomes.text: Use basic understanding of the knowledge of strategies in activity settings such as moving to open space to receive a pass or intercept an object.
Analyze and correct errors in movement patterns, and provide and use feedback from a peer or instruction technology.
Develop a cooperative movement game that uses locomotor skills, object manipulation, and an offensive strategy, and teach the game to another person.

Record and analyze food consumption for one day, and make a plan to replace foods with healthier choices.
Explain why dehydration impairs temperature regulation and physical and mental performance.

Perform flexibility exercises that will stretch particular muscles area for given physical activities.

outcomes.text: Identify, select, and participate in activities designed to improve selfdiagnosed areas for improvement in health-related fitness components.
Engage in moderate to vigorous physical activity at the target heart rate for a minimum of 60 minutes per day.
Accurately identify activities that are aerobic and anaerobic.
Determine the intensity of personal physical activity using the concept of perceived exertion.

topics.title: Recognize how health-related and skill-related fitness components contribute to a health-enhancing lifestyle that embraces physical fitness

subtopics.title: Recognize how health-related and skill-related fitness components contribute to a health-enhancing lifestyle that embraces physical fitness

outcomes.text: Monitor the intensity of one’s heart rate during physical activity
Identify target heart rate.
Explain how the six skill-related fitness components (agility, balance, eye-hand coordination, power, speed, reaction time) affect ability to enhance participation in activities.
Distinguish between health-related and skill-related fitness.
Identify activities that utilize enhanced skill-related components of fitness.
Compare results of fitness testing with research-based standards for self-improvement.

topics.title: Identify opportunities in school and in the community for regular participation in physical activity to enhance physical fitness

subtopics.title: Identify opportunities in school and in the community for regular participation in physical activity to enhance physical fitness

outcomes.text: Set age-appropriate fitness goals.
Strive to attain fitness goals through participation in physical activity of individual choosing
Identify where individuals can engage in regular physical activity to meet their personal fitness goals.

topics.title: Recognize diverse skill performance in self and in others and how diversity affects activities, games, and sport participation

outcomes.text: Evaluate individual responsibility in group efforts.
Accept differences among classmates in physical development, maturation and varying skill levels.
Participate in activities that address diversity with individuals of various skill levels.

topics.title: Choose to participate cooperatively and productively in group and individual physical activities

subtopics.title: Choose to participate cooperatively and productively in group and individual physical activities

outcomes.text: Help others with physical activity challenges.
Contribute ideas and listen to the ideas of others in cooperative problem solving activities.
Officiate an activity, game, or sport.
Demonstrate conflict resolution behavior in socially appropriate ways.
Demonstrate cooperation skills by establishing rules and guidelines for resolving conflicts.
Problem-solve with a small group of classmates during adventure activities, game play or team-building activities.

topics.title: Apply personal safety knowledge and skills to prevent and treat intentional or unintentional injury

subtopics.title: Apply personal safety knowledge and skills to prevent and treat intentional or unintentional injury

outcomes.text: Identify proper safety equipment for various physical activities.
Describe and demonstrate the correct form to push, pull, and lift heavy objects.
Identify appropriate footwear and sport-related gear/clothing for safe participation in various activities.
Create a list or poster that describes safety rules while participating in physical activities, with or without the help of an instructor.

topics.title: Combine the critical elements of movement and skills concepts

outcomes.text: Design and perform movement sequences that combine traveling, balancing, and weight transfer into smooth, flowing sequences with changes in direction, speed, and flow.
Cooperate with another student to create, develop, and refine movement routines based on a theme.
Create a game, movement, dance, or sport with a group.

outcomes.text: Analyze movement patterns, and correct errors.

topics.title: Demonstrate beginning offensive and defensive strategies for individual and team physical activities and sports

outcomes.text: Explain the principles of physical fitness (S.P.O.R.T.); Specificity, progression, overload, reversibility, and tedium.

topics.title: Demonstrates fitness knowledge and skills that maintain a health-enhancing lifestyle, while actively engaging in the participation of lifetime physical activities
